citation.excerpt: Requires a permitting agency to either approve or deny an application to create or serve an ADU or JADU within 60 days from when a completed application is received, if there is an existing single-family or multifamily dwelling on the lot. [...] Required a permitting agency to determine whether an application for an ADU or JADU is complete and provide written notice of the determination no later than 15 business days after the permitting agency received the application.

notes: Approved or denied without discretionary review or hearing (Gov. Code § 66317(a)). Completeness determination due within 15 business days (§ 66317(a)(2)(A), effective 2026); approval/denial within 60 days of a complete application. Denials must include a full written list of defective items and how to remedy them (§ 66317(b)). Encoded from the March 2026 HCD ADU Handbook; note SB 477 (2024) renumbered ADU law from § 65852.2 et seq. to §§ 66310–66342.

pathway: ADU — state-protected minimum unit (800 sq ft, 4-ft setbacks)

citation.excerpt: Prohibits a local agency from requiring "a zoning clearance or separate zoning review or any other minimum or maximum size for an accessory dwelling unit, size based upon a percentage of the proposed or existing primary dwelling, or limits on lot coverage, floor area ratio, open space, front setbacks, and minimum lot size, for either attached or detached dwellings that does not permit at least an 800 square foot accessory dwelling unit with four-foot side and rear yard setbacks to be constructed in compliance with all other local development standards."

notes: Local standards cannot preclude an 800 sq ft ADU with 4-foot side and rear setbacks. Useful as a floor when local objective standards appear to block a proposal.

citation.excerpt: Establishes a base height limitation of 16 feet for detached ADUs (Gov. Code, § 66321, subd. (b)(4)(A)). Increases the maximum height limitation on a detached ADU to 18 feet if the ADU is "either within a half-mile walking distance of a major transit stop or a high-quality transit corridor" and provides for an additional two feet for roof pitch [...] Establishes the maximum height limitation that may be imposed by a local agency on an attached ADU to 25 feet, or the existing primary dwelling height limit if lower than 25 feet.

notes: Detached: 16 ft base; 18 ft near a major transit stop / high-quality transit corridor or on a lot with an existing or proposed multistory multifamily dwelling; +2 ft for roof pitch matching the primary dwelling. Attached: up to 25 ft or the primary dwelling height limit if lower.

citation.excerpt: A unit that is no more than 500 square feet in interior livable space and contained entirely within a single-family residence. [...] if a JADU has shared sanitation facilities with the primary structure, owner-occupancy will be required. If the JADU does not have shared sanitation facilities, owner occupancy will not be required (Gov. Code, § 66333, subd. (b)). Additionally, made changes that stipulate JADUs can no longer be used as short-term rentals and, if rented, must now be rented for longer than 30 days (Gov. Code, § 66333, subd. (g)).

required_documents: floor plan showing the JADU within the single-family residence
notes: Max 500 sq ft interior livable space, contained entirely within the single-family residence. Owner-occupancy required only when sanitation facilities are shared (2025 legislation). Rentals must exceed 30 days.

citation.source: Gov. Code § 65852.21 — HCD Housing Law Fact Sheet: Duplexes and Lot Splits (SB 9), April 2026
citation.excerpt: SB 9 requires ministerial approval of a housing development with no more than two primary units in a single-family zone [...] local objective standards cannot preclude the development of one or two units of at least 800 square feet each on a qualifying lot. [...] Setbacks. A rear and side setback of up to four feet, except where there is an existing structure with less or no setback. [...] A complete application for a housing development or urban lot split must be approved or denied within 60 days from the date the local agency receives it.

notes: Up to two primary units, plus ADUs as permitted under ADU law. Exclusions encoded as intake screens: demolition/alteration of affordable-restricted, rent/price-controlled, or tenant-occupied (last 3 years) housing; Ellis Act withdrawals in last 15 years fall under protected housing; historic contributing structures/districts (AB 1061, 2025); environmentally sensitive/hazardous/protected sites per Gov. Code § 65913.4(a)(6)(B)–(K). Amended by SB 450 (2024) and AB 1061 (2025). Rentals must exceed 30 days.

citation.source: Gov. Code § 66411.7 — HCD Housing Law Fact Sheet: Duplexes and Lot Splits (SB 9), April 2026
citation.excerpt: the statute allows an applicant with a qualifying single-family lot to subdivide it into two lots of roughly equal size. [...] Local objective standards also cannot preclude the creation of two 1,200 square-foot lots. [...] an applicant for an urban lot split must sign an affidavit stating that the applicant intends to live in one of the units as their principal residence for at least three years from the date of approval of the urban lot split unless the applicant is a community land trust or nonprofit organization. [...] Parcels previously created under SB 9 lot split provisions are not eligible for further lot splits.

required_documents: owner-occupancy affidavit (3-year principal residence; exempt for community land trusts and nonprofits)
jurisdiction urban lot split application form
notes: Two lots of roughly equal size; objective standards cannot preclude two 1,200 sq ft lots. Up to two units allowed on each resulting lot. Jurisdictions may not require right-of-way dedication, offsite improvements, or correction of nonconforming conditions. Same site exclusions as the two-unit pathway, plus: no re-split of SB 9 lots and no split of parcels adjacent to a lot split by the same owner or someone acting in concert.

citation.source: Gov. Code §§ 66321(b)(2), 66314(d)(4)–(5); HSC § 17958.1 — HCD ADU Handbook (March 2026)
citation.excerpt: maximum unit size requirements must allow an ADU of at least 850 square feet of interior livable space, or 1,000 square feet of interior livable space for ADUs with more than one bedroom. (Gov. Code, § 66321, subd. (b)(2).) For local agencies without a compliant ADU ordinance, maximum unit sizes are 1,200 square feet of interior livable space for a new detached ADU (Gov. Code, § 66314, subd. (d)(4)) and up to 50 percent of the floor area of the existing primary dwelling for an attached ADU (at least 800 square feet of interior livable space) [...] The conversion of an existing accessory structure or a portion of the existing primary residence to an ADU is not subject to unit size requirements. (Gov. Code, § 66323, subd. (a)(1).)

notes: Local maximum sizes must allow at least 850 sq ft (or 1,000 sq ft for more than one bedroom) of interior livable space. Without a compliant local ordinance: 1,200 sq ft detached, 50% of primary dwelling floor area for attached (minimum 800 sq ft). No minimum size may prohibit an efficiency unit (as small as 150 sq ft, HSC § 17958.1). Conversions of existing space are not subject to size limits.

citation.excerpt: Parking requirements for ADUs shall not exceed one parking space per unit or bedroom, whichever is less (Gov. Code, § 66314, subd. (d)(10)(A)). These spaces may be provided as tandem parking on a driveway [...] Guest parking spaces shall not be required for ADUs under any circumstances. [...] a local agency may not require off-street parking spaces to be replaced when a garage, carport, covered parking structure, or uncovered parking space is demolished in conjunction with the construction of an ADU [...] A local agency shall not impose parking standards on any of the following ADUs, pursuant to Government Code section 66322, subdivision (a): 1) ADUs located within one-half mile walking distance of public transit.

notes: Maximum one space per unit or bedroom, whichever is less; tandem on a driveway counts; guest parking never required. Full exemptions (§ 66322(a)): within half-mile walk of public transit; in an architecturally/historically significant district; ADU part of the primary residence or accessory structure; on-street permits required but not offered to the ADU occupant; car-share vehicle within a block. Demolished garage/carport parking need not be replaced.

pathway: ADU — no owner-occupancy requirement; rental terms

citation.excerpt: Only ADUs which are sold separately to a qualified buyer under Government Code section 66341, subdivision (c)(3), can require owner-occupancy. Otherwise, a local agency cannot impose an owner-occupancy requirement on any other ADU (Gov. Code, § 66315). [...] Local agencies may require that ADUs and JADUs be rented for terms longer than 30 days (Gov. Code, § 66315; 66323, subd. (e); 66333, subd. (g)).

notes: A jurisdiction cannot require the owner to live on the property to permit an ADU (narrow exception: separate-conveyance sales under § 66341(c)(3)). Jurisdictions may require rental terms longer than 30 days — no short-term rentals.

pathway: ADU — conversion of existing space (setback and standards exemptions)

citation.excerpt: No setback shall be required for an ADU or JADU created within an existing living area or accessory structure or an ADU created in a new structure in the same location and to the same dimensions as an existing structure (Gov. Code, § 66314, subd. (d)(7)). [...] Objective standards related to height, lot coverage, landscape, design, development, and architectural standards in the local ADU ordinance do not apply to ADU conversions. [...] ADU conversions are not subject to setback requirements because they are created within an existing living area or are constructed in the same location and to the same dimensions as an existing structure.

notes: Converting existing space (garage, accessory structure, part of the house) or rebuilding in the same location and dimensions: no setback requirements, and local height/lot-coverage/design standards do not apply. Conversions remain subject to building, health and safety, and fire codes.

pathway: ADU — legalizing an unpermitted unit built before 2020

citation.excerpt: A local agency shall not deny a permit for an unpermitted ADU that was constructed before January 1, 2020, due to the ADU being in violation of building standards, non-compliance with State ADU Law, or any local ordinance regulating ADUs (Gov. Code, § 66311.7, subd. (a)). However, the local agency may deny the permit if the local agency makes a finding that correcting the violation is necessary to protect the health and safety of the public or occupants of the structure, or if the building is deemed substandard pursuant to section 17920.3 of the Health and Safety Code.

required_documents: permit application for the existing unit
optional: confidential third-party code inspection report from a licensed contractor (Gov. Code § 66311.7(d)(2))
notes: Units built before January 1, 2020 without permits can generally be legalized: denial requires specific health-and-safety or substandard-building findings. The agency must publish a checklist of substandard conditions (HSC § 17920.3) and inform homeowners they may obtain a confidential third-party inspection before applying.

citation.excerpt: Under Government Code section 66323, an applicant may apply to build up to eight detached ADUs (Gov. Code, § 66323, subd. (a)(4)(A)) and at least one conversion ADU within an existing multifamily dwelling and up to 25 percent of the number of units in the existing multifamily dwelling (Gov. Code, § 66323, subd. (a)(3)(B)).

required_documents: site plan showing existing multifamily structure and proposed ADU locations
notes: On a lot with an existing multifamily dwelling: up to eight detached ADUs (not exceeding the number of existing units on the lot; 16-ft height limit and 4-ft rear/side setbacks apply), plus conversion ADUs in non-livable space (storage rooms, passageways) up to 25% of existing unit count. 66323 Units are exempt from local design/development standards not specified in § 66323.

pathway: SB 9 + ADU law — how unit counts combine

citation.source: Gov. Code §§ 65852.21, 66411.7 + State ADU Law — HCD ADU Handbook (March 2026)
citation.excerpt: When a lot split occurs, SB 9 requires the local agency to approve up to two units on each parcel but specifically states that only two units are allowed per parcel, despite what ADU Law would otherwise allow. Those two units could be two primary "SB 9 units," or one primary unit and one ADU, or one primary unit and one JADU. [...] When an SB 9 lot split has not occurred, the lot is eligible to receive up to two primary units under SB 9, as well as whatever combination of ADUs and JADUs it would otherwise be entitled to under ADU Law.

notes: After an SB 9 lot split: hard cap of two units per resulting parcel (any mix of primary units, ADU, or JADU). Without a lot split: two primary units plus normal ADU/JADU entitlements — but if that combination exceeds four total units, the agency is not required to also approve a lot split.
